summary: The arbitrary-selected-mass construction is valid. The metronoid depth bound gives each cap fiber volume at least gamma_d t_z; the segment-to-an-interior-point arguments correctly prove that every individual cap and every strictly positive same-base reweighting is full-dimensional; Brunn-Minkowski gives the claimed reweighted fiber and total-mass bounds; positive rescaling of directions and affine minorants preserves the cap halfspaces, balance, negativity, exactness at m, and global support-minimal cardinality; vertex optimality yields affinely independent contact sets, and the strict-superlevel density argument correctly proves the contact upper bound f_i(z) <= t_z. For degree-saturated matching masses t_z=2d_z(p), endpoint double counting gives T=4P, scaling p by gamma_d satisfies every new degree capacity, and all factors 2, 4, 2^{-n}, gamma_d, and the strict gamma_d>1/e comparison match. The final paragraph correctly limits legal balanced-cap-descendant status to the additional half-mass hypotheses and asserts no descendant-specific consequences for general selected masses.
